cards.text: The people just heard God speak, and they were so scared they stood at a distance while Moses, Israel's leader, approached the thick darkness where God was (Exodus 20:18-21). Now the LORD gives Moses a message for the Israelites. It opens with something they've seen for themselves.

cards.question: God reminds the Israelites they've seen for themselves that He spoke to them. Where did He speak from?
God has spoken to them straight from heaven. Next, what does He say they must not make for themselves?

answers.text: a king to rule over them
a tower that reaches the sky

cards.text: What they ARE to make is an altar of earth for their burnt offerings and peace offerings. DIRT, friend, and as a stamper who came out of a clearance bin for a quarter, that's my kind of building project.

cards.question: In every place where God causes His name to be remembered, He promises to come to them and ___ them.
If they build the altar out of stones instead, God wants those stones carefully cut and shaped with tools.

cards.text: One more altar rule: no going up to God's altar on steps, so nobody's nakedness is exposed on it. Friend, I wear a full apron just to stamp COOKIES, so you won't hear me argue with that one.

Then the LORD gives Moses ordinances for everyday life: how to treat servants, what's owed when someone gets hurt or an ox gores, and how to care for foreigners, widows, orphans and the poor. There's even a rule to help the donkey of someone who hates you when it falls under its load, plus the famous rule of eye for eye and tooth for tooth. Three chapters of rules, and not ONE about sneaking cookie dough off the counter. I looked.

cards.question: After all those laws, God tells them to pay close attention to everything He's said. Then what must never be heard on their lips?

cards.text: Last come the feasts: three times a year they celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Harvest and the Feast of Ingathering, and three times a year all their males appear before the Lord GOD. A few offering rules close it out, like bringing the best of the firstfruits to the house of the LORD, but keep your apron on, friend, because this conversation isn't finished.

findings.problem: Most of the stop's choices depend on discovering unseen wording or details rather than reasoning from the setup. Cards 2 and 3 ask for answers that cannot be inferred from card 1, card 5 asks for an unseen word, and card 6 gives no dependable basis for choosing between shaped and unshaped stones. With four of the five choices working this way, the stop goes beyond the allowed few discovery questions. Add context that supports reasoned picks or replace some questions.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the unseen final word of Exodus 20:24. The preceding story card discusses the altar but does not establish the promise, so the baker is guessing the verse's wording rather than reasoning out its meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Choice cards 3, 5, 6 and 9 refer to the Israelites only as 'them' or 'they,' without identifying the group within the question. Since the preceding story card is no longer on screen, each question needs to identify who God is addressing.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has four sentences: the summary, the donkey and eye-for-eye details, the cookie-dough sentence, and 'I looked.' Condense it to no more than two sentences while retaining the long-stretch summary.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
